Official_Learning_Outcome: Describe the characteristics of living things.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded direct concept

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise some broad groups of living things based on similarities and differences.
Observe a variety of living and non-living things and infer differences between them.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Anything that moves is a living thing.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Classify living things into broad groups (in plants and animals) based on similarities and differences of common observable characteristics.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Relate the use of various types of materials (wood, metal, ceramic, rubber, glass, plastic, fabric) to their physical properties.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application targeting: Objects are made of only one type of material.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Compare physical properties of materials.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: All plastic objects float on water.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Show an understanding that different living things have different life cycles.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: The first stage of each life cycle is the egg.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Observe and compare the life cycles of plants grown from seeds over a period of time.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Observe and compare the life cycles of animals over a period of time (chicken, cockroach, frog, grasshopper, beetle, butterfly, mosquito).
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: All insects have the same life cycle.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that a magnet can exert a push or a pull.
Identify the characteristics of magnets.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded direct concept | Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Bigger magnets are stronger than smaller magnets.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise uses of magnets in everyday objects.
Compare magnets, non-magnetic materials and magnetic materials.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application targeting: An object is a magnet if it attracts another magnet.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Make a magnet by the stroke method and the electrical method.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Identify the different parts of plants and state their functions.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Plants obtain their 'food' from the soil through their roots. | Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Plants take in water through the leaves instead of the roots.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Observe plant parts.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Identify the human systems in the body and state their functions (digestive, respiratory, circulatory, skeletal and muscular).
Identify the parts in the human digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine) and describe their functions.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Digestion begins in the stomach. | Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: State that matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
Differentiate among the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) in terms of shape and volume.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe

Official_Learning_Outcome: Measure mass and volume using appropriate apparatus.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that an object can be seen when it reflects light or when it is a source of light.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Only smooth, shiny objects like mirrors reflect light; dull and rough objects do not reflect light.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that light travels in straight lines and thus a shadow is formed when light is completely or partially blocked by an object.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Shadow is matter.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Investigate the variables that affect shadows formed.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Identify some common sources of heat.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Objects that keep us warm are sources of heat.

Official_Learning_Outcome: State that the temperature of an object is a measurement of its degree of hotness.
State that heat is a form of energy.
Differentiate between heat and temperature.
Show an understanding that heat flows from a hotter to a colder object/ region/ place until both reach the same temperature.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Coldness travels.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Relate the change in temperature of an object to the gain or loss of heat by the object.
List some effects of heat gain/loss in our everyday life.
Identify good and poor conductors of heat.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Poor conductors of heat help to keep things cool only, while good conductors help to keep things warm only.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Measure temperature using a thermometer and a datalogger with temperature/heat sensors.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that a cell is a basic unit of life.
Strengthening_Note: Replaced 2 cell-part questions that exceeded the TLG assessment scope with basic-unit-of-life / growth probes.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Show an understanding that living things reproduce to ensure continuity of their kind and that many characteristics of an organism are passed on from parents to offspring.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Offspring inherits certain characteristics from one parent, and other characteristics from another parent.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Describe processes in the sexual reproduction of flowering plants.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise the process of fertilisation in the sexual reproduction of humans.
Recognise the similarity in terms of fertilisation in the sexual reproduction of flowering plants and humans.
Investigate the ways in which plants reproduce.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application targeting: All plants reproduce by seeds.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that water can exist in three interchangeable states of matter.
Show an understanding of how water changes from one state to another.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Evaporation only occurs when water is boiling or when there is a direct heat source.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Show an understanding of the terms melting point of ice (or freezing point of water) and boiling point of water.
Show an understanding of the roles of evaporation and condensation in the water cycle.
Recognise the importance of the water cycle.
Recognise the importance of water to life processes.
Describe the impact of water pollution on Earth’s water resources.
Compare water in 3 states.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Investigate the effect of heat gain or loss on the temperature and state of water.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: The temperature changes continuously during a change of state.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Investigate the factors which affect the rate of evaporation.
Identify the parts of the plant transport system and describe their functions.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Water-carrying tubes are found only in stems.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Investigate how food and water are transported in the plant.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that air is made up of gases such as nitrogen, carbon dioxide, oxygen and water vapour.
Identify the parts of the human respiratory (nose, windpipe, lungs) and circulatory systems (heart, blood, blood vessels) and describe their functions.
Recognise the integration of the different systems (digestive, respiratory and circulatory) in carrying out life processes.
Compare how plants, fish and humans take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Compare the ways in which substances are transported within plants and humans.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that an electric circuit consisting of an energy source (battery) and other circuit components (wire, bulb, switch) forms an electrical system.
Show an understanding that a closed circuit allows current to flow.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: In an open circuit, current flows to the part where there is a gap and 'turns back' to the battery.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Identify electrical conductors and insulators.
Construct simple circuits from circuit diagrams.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Investigate the effect of some variables on the current in a circuit.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application | Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Brightness of each bulb decreases when an additional bulb is connected in parallel circuits.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that living things need energy from respiration to carry out life processes.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Respiration is the same as breathing.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Recognise that the Sun is our primary source of energy (light and heat).
Differentiate between the ways in which plants and animals obtain energy.
Investigate the requirements (water, light energy and carbon dioxide) for photosynthesis (production of sugar and oxygen).
Recognise that energy from most of our energy resources is derived in some ways from the Sun.
Recognise and give examples of the various forms of energy.
Investigate energy conversion from one form to another.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Forces and energy are the same. Energy can be converted into forces.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Identify a force as a push or a pull.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded misconception/application probe targeting: Force only involves objects that are in contact with one another.

Official_Learning_Outcome: Show an understanding of the effects of a force.
Recognise and give examples of the different types of forces.
Recognise that objects have weight because of the gravitational force acting on the object.
Investigate the effect of frictional force on the motion of objects.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Investigate the effects of elastic spring force.
Strengthening_Note: Added TLG-grounded application

Official_Learning_Outcome: Identify the factors that affect the survival of an organism.
Show an understanding of the effect on organisms when the environment becomes unfavourable (organisms adapt and survive; move to other places or die).
Show an understanding of the energy pathway from the Sun through living things and identify the roles of various organisms (producers, consumers, predators, prey) in a food chain and a food web.
Differentiate among organism, population and community.
Show an understanding that different habitats support different communities (garden, field, pond, seashore, tree, mangrove swamp).
Show an understanding that adaptations serve to enhance survival and can be structural or behavioural.
Give examples of man’s impact (both positive and negative) on the environment.
Observe, collect and record information regarding the interacting factors within an environment.
